findings.title: Reconcile 日 sense evidence and review history
findings.details: The final 日 article has matching current senses and has_sense edges for sun, daylight, the day unit, and Japan abbreviation, supported by present-day Chinese dictionaries; it excludes the Japanese-only day-counter gloss. Earlier review rounds repeatedly rejected or reversed these claims, while the final factual and readability reviews passed. Preserve the final dictionary-backed treatment and ensure future repairs check current dictionary senses before treating them as unsupported or historical.
findings.verification: Inspect any later 日 revision against the cited current Chinese dictionary evidence, verify sense status and generated has_sense edges agree, and confirm Japanese-only glosses are not imported as Chinese senses.
evidence: actual_findings round-0 through round-3 factual/readability reviews

findings.title: Keep 日 bronze redraw provenance qualified
findings.details: The article describes the selected glyph as a modern redraw attributed to a mid-Western Zhou bronze form and explicitly says the image-to-inscription match is unverified. The dossier also records that the SVG pixels were not visually inspected in this invocation. Earlier review rounds identified unsupported exact vessel attribution and shape description; final caption and alt text qualify the provenance and describe the visible shape, but the redraw-to-inscription match remains unresolved.
findings.verification: If the glyph is reused or its visual claim is strengthened, inspect the actual vector and verify its match to the cited inscription; retain the distinction between database attribution and image-to-specimen verification.
